q: gerthardus lodewikus booysen - - - · booyzen the one document that names him has been weakened, and by somebody who had not seen it. on 14 september 2026 pieter van zyl, answering this archive's g2g question, guessed that the 1876 informant had reached for a name already in the household - and added, from memory, that he thought a child of petrus jacobus was called gerhardus lodewicus. he is right, and the child is on the same sheet: line 12 of that very notice names jan gerthardus lodewikus booijsen among the eight children. so the name this archive takes from line 3, for the dead man's father, is the back half of his son's name, eight lines below, in one clerk's hand - and the half that is dropped, jan, is the name de villiers gives as the real father. this does not prove the father was jan and this archive is not swapping one unproved father for another. it removes the only document that has ever carried this name from the evidence for him. the top of the male line is now held up by less than it was this morning. he still has no birth date, no death date, and no parents: the oldest open question on this site is about him. 15 september 2026 - and the last escape route is closed. this archive's standing objection was that de villiers's 1893 original was revised by pama in 1981, and a revision can move a man; if the 1981 edition had relocated petrus jacobus, the death notice would stand. riel smit, who has the 1981 edition: "yes, de villiers & pama (1981) still place petrus jacobus (b3c4d7) b. 21 sept 1788 under jan b3c4." pieter van zyl adds that he searched for a marriage between a gerhardus lodewicus and a magdalena de beer and could not find one. four things now point one way and the only thing pointing the other is line 3 of notice 678. the spine is still not being moved on this: everything against him is a printed genealogy agreeing with its own earlier edition, and what he has is a primary document signed by a son. what ends it is the baptism entry of 21 september 1788 - the register de villiers compiled his entry from, naming the father in a contemporary hand. it is now the first item on the errands page. 

jan booijsen bapt. 29 jan 1741 - bef. c. 1836 · booyzen the man the book puts where the document puts somebody else. b3c4 - son of gerrit booijsen and johanna du rand; burgher at drakenstein; married magdalena de beer 21 january 1770 and remarried margaretha pretorius 15 december 1793, which is how this archive knows the de beer wife was dead by then. de villiers (1893) gives him twelve children, of whom d5 is jan jonathan, d6 magdalena and d7 petrus jacobus, baptised 21 september 1788 - this archive's own ancestor. riel smit confirms that de villiers & pama (1981) still places him there. pieter van zyl notes he was dead more than forty years before petrus jacobus died in 1876, which is why the grandson who signed the death notice could write somebody else's name in the parents' box. he is entered as inferred and not as documented, because two editions of one printed genealogy are one source agreeing with itself, and the primary document on this site says gerthardus lodewikus. the baptism register of 21 september 1788 decides between them. 

magdelena elisabeth de beer 1754 - 1843 · booyzen wife of gerthardus lodewikus. her 1754 birth is what dates him at all - and her name, beside his, is what the 1876 notice puts on the record. that matters because a 1793 cape will names a different "jan booysen, married to the late magdalena de beer": the pairing was never unique, and now this line's version of it is documented. magdelenaelisabethdebeer17541843booyzenwifeofgertharduslodewikusher1754birthiswhatdateshimatallandhernamebesidehisiswhatthe1876noticeputsontherecordthatmattersbecausea1793capewillnamesadifferentjanbooysenmarriedtothelatemagdalenadebeerthepairingwasneveruniqueandnowthislinesversionofitisdocumented

s: c. 21 Sep 1788, Graaff-Reinet – 1 Sep 1876, district Rustenburg · Booyzen
q: petrus jacobus booysen c. 21 sep 1788, graaff-reinet - 1 sep 1876, district rustenburg · booyzen married at about seventeen; died a widower in the transvaal, eighty-eight years old, on a farm called brakfontein. his sterfkennis - no. 678, written 14 september 1876 - is the oldest document about this family that this archive has read, it names his parents, and it lists eight children. estate: nothing. "niets nagelaten. niets bekend." 

david schalk booijsen 12 dec 1806, baptised 4 jan 1807 - - · booyzen first on his father's 1876 death notice, and a major - and now with a date. his baptism of 4 january 1807 names his parents as pieter jacobus booijzen and anna maria van der merwe, which is the only document in this archive that puts anna maria in the family at all. his father was eighteen when he was born. he married adriana christina viljoen - on 3 november 1828 at cradock, a date and a place this archive did not have until wikitree was read on 13 september 2026, and from wikitree, not from a document this archive has read - and named a daughter anna maria in 1835, after his own mother. his nephew, born 1848, carries the same name - the two are told apart only by a generation. 

magdalena booijsen of 1782 bapt. 29 sep 1782 - - · booyzen b3c4d6 - sister of petrus jacobus, the man at the head of this archive's documented line, and six years older. de villiers's volume 1 records her marriage only as "gehuwd met h. a. viljoen"; volume 3 gives it in full from the viljoen side - hercules albertus viljoen, baptised 30 march 1777, burgher at graaff-reinet, married 26 february 1797. seven children, of whom the seventh is adriana christina, baptised 19 august 1810 - the name and the age of the woman her nephew david schalk married at cradock in 1828. if that is the same woman, this aunt is also a mother-in-law. 

jan jonathan booijsen bapt. 11 jul 1779 - - · booyzen b3c4d5 - the eldest of the three siblings whose marriages braid this family into the viljoens. burgher at graaff-reinet; married 28 may 1797 to judith cornelia theresia viljoen, three months after his sister magdalena married that woman's brother hercules albertus. a brother and a sister married a sister and a brother in one year. seven children, and the sixth is judith cornelia theresia, baptised 16 august 1807 - b3c4d5e6, the code this archive resolved last week to settle a johannesburg gravestone. she carries her mother's three names entire, and her mother was a viljoen. 

adriana christina viljoen - - - · booyzen his wife, married at cradock on 3 november 1828-from wikitree, not from a document this archive has read-and named with him on their daughter anna maria's baptism of 13 september 1835 - a daughter called after his mother, which is how this archive knows the naming ran that way in this generation too. and she was probably his first cousin. de villiers, volume 3, under villion, thans viljoen: "(e) 12 hercules albertus, gedoopt 30 maart 1777, burger te graaff-reinet, gehuwd 26 februari 1797 met magdalena booijsen", and their seventh child is "adriana christina, gedoopt 19 augustus 1810". magdalena booijsen is b3c4d6, the sister of petrus jacobus - david schalk's own father. that makes adriana christina eighteen in 1828 and makes him her first cousin. not proved: de villiers records her baptism and gives her no husband, and the 1828 cradock date is itself only on wikitree. right name, right age, right district, and a family already tied twice - but the weak join is the marriage record this archive has never seen.

david schalk booysen 9 jun 1848, cradock - after nov 1905 · booyzen prisoner of war. a printed transport list in the pretoria government archives, image group 008019246, carries three consecutive booyzens shipped on the city of cambridge on 3 june 1901, all entered from pretoria: 18463 stephanus francois, 28 · 18464 petrus jacobus, 29 · 18465 david schalk, 54. consecutive numbers on one transport means taken together. age 54 against a birth of 9 june 1848, which would have made him 52 and six days short of 53 when the ship sailed. the fuller register was then found, and it is better than the de list in every respect: item 1 of the same film, image 126, gives all three as living at pretoria, riding with the pretoria commando, and taken at tolosberg on 25 april 1901. its ages are 26, 27 and 53, which match this archive's own dates where the de list's 28, 29 and 54 did not. if it is him, he was a transvaal burgher in arms at fifty-two, taken and deported, and he came back - he remarried at pretoria in november 1905. fourth on the 1863 list, and the direct ancestor's brother - willem hermanus is sixth on the same list. for the whole of this project he was a line on that list and nothing else. his wife's 1900 death notice gives him a household: married elizabetha margaretha marais at lady grey, the same small cape church where his brother married kathleen barry in 1879; eight children; and by 1900 he was at pretoria, living in a zinc building in market street. he signed her notice there in march 1904 - and on 27 november 1905 he married again at pretoria, to johanna elena stols, widow lowies, of skinners court. he was 56, a widower of goede hoop, pretoria, and the register gives his birthplace as cradock. the remarks column cites his remarriage certificate from the master, no. 4795 - which is the number of his first wife's death notice, so the two documents point at each other and the identification needs no inference. his own death is still not found.

s: c. Oct 1874, Cape Province – 14 May 1940, East Lynne, Pretoria · Booyzen
q: stephanus francois booyzen c. oct 1874, cape province - 14 may 1940, east lynne, pretoria · booyzen the stone is now read, and it is the fullest document this archive has for him. silverton, pretoria, a double stone under one base reading booyzen: "'n simbool van liefde - aan my dierbare eggenoot en ons vader - stefanus francois - ✳ 29-9-1874, † 14-5-1940 - sy plek is leeg, sy stem is stil, ons swyg o'heer, dit is gods wil. ges. 75:1". his birth is now exact: 29 september 1874, where this archive had only "c. october 1874". and a pillar between the two halves lists twelve children by their household names - ouboet · ousie · bessie · betie · henna · evert · ✝baba · fanie · willie · pietie · johan · hennie - one of them marked dead with a cross. this archive had almost none of them. they are nicknames, not names on a register, and nothing is claimed from them beyond the count. his grave is found and photographed: "booyzen stefanus francois 1874-1940", silverton main cemetery, pretoria - a joint stone with his wife, "booyzen beatrix magdalena catharina nee boshoff 1889-1977". both dates match this archive exactly, and hers is the first death year it has had for her. he died at east lynne, pretoria, and lies at silverton. image located, not yet read. prisoner of war. a printed transport list in the pretoria government archives, image group 008019246, carries three consecutive booyzens shipped on the city of cambridge on 3 june 1901, all entered from pretoria: 18463 stephanus francois, 28 · 18464 petrus jacobus, 29 · 18465 david schalk, 54. consecutive numbers on one transport means taken together. age 28 against this archive's c. october 1874, which would have made him 26. the fuller register was then found, and it is better than the de list in every respect: item 1 of the same film, image 126, gives all three as living at pretoria, riding with the pretoria commando, and taken at tolosberg on 25 april 1901. its ages are 26, 27 and 53, which match this archive's own dates where the de list's 28, 29 and 54 did not. and then the prisoner number led somewhere else entirely. the medal-roll database at angloboerwar.com holds an entry for a stephanus francois booysen, burger, whose pow number is 18463 - the same number as the register - and it says he was a zarp, one of the zar's police, based at pretoria. quoting a city coins auction catalogue of november 2020 that described his abo medal and the papers with it: in action at talana, modder spruit, colenso, platrand (wagon hill) where he was wounded in the right leg above the knee, spion kop and dalmanutha - the zarps' famous last stand. his applications were completed by his commanding officer, commandant j. p. de la c. schroeder. he was one of forty-two boers taken at tolosberg in the waterval valley on 25 april 1901, with two guns and much stock, and was sent to india. this archive has not seen the medal or the application; it is strong secondary evidence tied to the register by the number and not by the name. what it does to the dispute: he is numbered 18463 and david schalk booysen is 18465, two apart on the same transport on the same day, and this man died at east lynne, pretoria, which is the district all three were taken in. that is a fourth point favouring david schalk as his father, and the first that does not depend on a forename. it is still not a document naming a parent. parentage disputed - see below. a son of the second marriage, and a messelaar - a mason, like his half-brother willem hermanus at indwe. his 1940 sterfkennis was fetched because it should have named his mother; his widow wrote only "oorlede" for both parents. married beatrix magdalena catharina boshoff at mosselbaai on 5 september 1905, certificate 1318 - he 30 and a jonkman, she sixteen with her parents consenting. eleven children; left immovable property and a will. the register gives his residence as pretoria, and eleven weeks later david schalk booijzen of goede hoop, pretoria - whose 1900 notice names an unmarried major son called stephanus francois - remarried in that same city. this archive placed him under petrus jacobus on his birth year alone. it is marked serious on the disputed page and it is not decided.

james montjoy c. 1782, "europe" - sep 1827, cradock · mountjoy saddler. owned a house and erf at cradock worth £90. his 1840 death notice gives his parents as not known - the oldest document here, and the top of this line. 15 september 2026 - a man who slept in his house says where he came from. john montgomery, founder of burgersdorp, in the friend of the free state of 25 november 1869, recalling his arrival at cradock in january 1822 when the place held about six people: "messrs. solomon and s.m. de beer, the rev. mr. evans, mr. p. gie, james mountjoy (a saddler, who was discharged from the 21st light dragoons), the two messrs. ziervogel, mr. heilberg, fieldcornet b.j. vorster, and gert van deventer. after some trouble i obtained lodgings for the night from mr. mountjoy." there is no room in a village of six for two saddlers of one name. the 21st light dragoons were the cavalry of the cape garrison from the 1806 expedition until the end of that decade, so he arrived in uniform - which is exactly why no cape document can say where he was from, and why the marriage register of 1817 rules a line through the column and leaves it empty. he was not a passenger on anything. the record that answers it is wo 97 at kew, the chelsea discharge papers, arranged by regiment before 1855, which give a soldier's parish and county of birth, his age at enlistment and his trade. 16 september 2026 - his discharge now has a deadline, and it came from the london papers. the 21st light dragoons were relieved at york in may 1806 and sailed from portsmouth for the cape; part of them went on to south america in 1806 and came back to the cape in 1807; parliament complained in march 1809 that they had been sent "where they could have nothing to do"; a large reinforcement followed in october 1810; sir john cradock reviewed them and pronounced them "in the highest state of discipline"; a draft of 140 men embarked for the cape in october 1813; and then, in a letter from the cape dated 1 and 10 september 1817 and printed in five london papers that november, "the 21st light dragoons have embarked for india". he married at graaff-reinet on 9 march 1817. his regiment sailed for india six months later. a man who married in march 1817 and was keeping a house and a saddler's trade at cradock by january 1822 was discharged at the cape before september 1817, and what he was choosing between was a wife at graaff-reinet and a transport to madras. the town he settled in is named after the governor who reviewed his regiment. 

anna catharina sleer bapt. 14 oct 1787 - 1885 · mountjoy lived to ninety-eight. married james montjoy 9 mar 1817 at graaff-reinet, having first been the widow of a pietersen. 15 september 2026 - she has parents, a baptism and three siblings. de villiers's volume 3, entry 876: "willem slier, van hamburg, gehuwd 19 november 1780 met anna catharina fortman - (b) 1 anna catharina, gedoopt 14 october 1787, gehuwd met hermanus pieterse; 2 wilhelmina christina, gedoopt 27 december 1789, gehuwd 5 januari 1811 met jan abraham van wijk, van amsterdam; 3 geertruida johanna, gedoopt 2 juli 1791; 4 wilhelmus josephus, gedoopt 5 maart 1797." and the five spellings stop being a mystery: a hamburg name - schlier, schleer - written down by cape clerks who had never seen it. she married hermanus pietersen on 5 april 1807 at nineteen, was a widow by march 1817, a widow again by september 1827, and lived until 1885. fifty-eight years a widow.

hermanus pietersen - - bef. mar 1817 · mountjoy anna catharina slier's first husband, and until today this archive had him and his son as one man. de villiers, volume 3: "hermanus pietersen, namen van ouders onbekend, gehuwd 5 april 1807 met anna catharina slier - (b) 1 willem hermanus, gedoopt 12 maart 1809; 2 johan christiaan, gedoopt 28 april 1810." the entry here used to read "willem hermanus pieterzen, her first husband", built from two documents that spell him differently - the 1817 marriage register's harmanus pieterze and the 1840 death notice's william pietersen - and two spellings looked like one long name. they are a father and a son. his own parents were unknown to the book, as james montjoy's would be to the clerk ten years later: two men in one woman's life and neither of them had a recorded father. 

willem hermanus pietersen bapt. 12 mar 1809 - - · mountjoy the son, not the husband - and the man the name in this family actually comes from. baptised 12 march 1809, the elder of anna catharina slier's two pietersen boys, and so half-brother to the montjoy children. he stood godfather at the 1851 graaff-reinet font, where his surname is written pieterzen twice in the same hand that wrote booyzen three lines above - the entry that taught this archive that a z is dutch orthography and not intent. his name is his two grandfathers and his father: willem for willem slier of hamburg, hermanus for hermanus pietersen.

q: james henry barry 13 jul 1848, baptised 13 nov 1848 at graaff-reinet - 23 jun 1939, barkly east · barry settled, 14 september 2026, and it removes a candidate rather than adding one. the henry jaonas barry who turned up on 13 september - "baptised at twenty years old" in 1868, and briefly a candidate for a tenth child - is this man. the same event is indexed twice: once as henry jaonas barry, baptism 13 nov 1868, and once as hennery james berry, baptism 13 nov 1848. same birth date of 13 july 1848, same parents, same collection, and familysearch attaches both to one tree person, james henry barry 1848-1939. the volume decides the year on its own: the register is "graaff-reinet. baptism records 1846-1851", and a baptism of 1868 cannot sit in a book that closes in 1851. so he was baptised at four months, not at twenty, at graaff-reinet - not at cape town or tulbagh, which is what both index entries say for the place. the birth-spacing argument made against him held: his brother john augustus ii was born 13 march 1847 and he was born sixteen months later. the image has been located and not read - identifier apid:th-909-70517-31299-17. named on the 1915 death notice, which he swore himself. the index now dates him: born about 1847, dead at barkly east on 23 june 1939, having outlived his father by thirty-six years. but that year cannot stand. his brother john augustus barry ii was born 13 march 1847 off a register, and "about 1847" here is not a date at all - it is an age worked back from the 1939 death. two brothers cannot share it. a relationship search on his mother's surname turned up a henry jaonas barry born 13 july 1848 and baptised at twenty, which is where a next child belongs; whether that is this man under a clerk's ear is unproved and the register is unread.

richard pieter kolbe barry 1899 - - · barry and the name is in a government file, twice over, in one line. sab, vwr volume 2, reference b645/8/38, 1937: "aansoek deur plaaseienaar barkly-oos. rpk barry. bywoner rpk barry (seun)." an application by a farm owner at barkly east - r.p.k. barry - and the bywoner on the place is r.p.k. barry, his son. two men of these initials at barkly east in 1937, one holding the land and one working it as a tenant, and the state file is between them. this archive cannot say which of the two is the man born in 1899 and does not guess. a bywoner is not a labourer and not an owner; it is the word south africa used in the 1930s for a white tenant farming another man's ground, and vwr is the department of social welfare. the file has not been read. carries both names at once - richard pieter, for the barry of manorowen, and kolbe, for the 1820 settler family his great-grandmother married out of. married maria magdalena siebert. from the index; no image read.

johanna catharina mountjoy of indwe - - jun 1911, indwe · mountjoy she joined the dutch reformed congregation at indwe on 23 july 1907, arriving from barkly oost - six weeks after willem hermanus booijzen was confirmed in the same church - and the register's last column records her dead there in june 1911. a mountjoy and a booyzen in one small colliery congregation, twenty-two years after the two families stood at the same font at barkly oost. 15 september 2026 - and there is now a candidate birth date, not entered. the baptism transcriptions indexed by gendatabase.com hold a johanna catharina mountjoy born 28 january 1860, one of four mountjoy children baptised between 1858 and 1864. she would be fifty-one in june 1911. it is not being taken: this family already contains a johanna catharina mountjoy born 1819, so the name repeats within it, and what would decide it is the congregation the 1860 baptism was registered in - which is the field that site charges for. if it is barkly east or its district, the two women are almost certainly one. 17 september 2026 - and she has a joining date. the indwe lidmate register enters her on 23 july 1907 - familysearch 1:1:6pr3-hnwz - seven weeks after willem hermanus booijzen was confirmed in the same congregation on 31 may 1907. this archive had her death at indwe and nothing before it. it does not make the two families relatives; it makes them neighbours, in one small coal town's register, in one winter.

q: henry james kolbe barry barkly east - 1958 - estate nab msce 2183/1958 · barry new, and he carries the whole argument in his name. "barry, henry james kolbe. born in barkly east, cape province. unmarried. deceased estate", pietermaritzburg archives repository, msce 2183/1958. henry james is the barry forename this archive has followed since 1848; kolbe is the surname it has spent the project proving is the source of half the family's given names. here they are in one man, born in this archive's own town, dying unmarried in natal in 1958 - so the names stop with him. he is the third barry found carrying kolbe as a forename, after richard pieter kolbe barry and anton rector kolbe barry. no parents named; the estate is not read. 

margrith louisa maria barry bapt. 5 apr 1852, burgersdorp - - · barry one of the two missing barry children, found 16 september 2026 - and open question 13 has been asking for her since this site was written. the 1903 registration of her father's death says eleven children; his own death notice names eight and her mother's names nine. she is in the burgersdorp register and not in any name search, because the index gives her no surname: two separate index passes of the same page read "margrith louisa maria" and "margreth louisa mary", and the name column stops there. it is the blank name column again, the same failure that hid her sister catherine mary sophia of 1855. found by asking the index for a relationship - father john barry, mother a kolbe - and letting it return whatever the child was called. her parents are entered as "margrith willemina kolbe + john barry". she is almost certainly the "margaret mary" named on her parents' death notices and never placed: it is her mother's name, and there is no other candidate in the sibling group. ark:/61903/1:1:6vyg-ss94 and 1:1:6f4l-76pk. 

william frederick thomas barry 29 sep 1861, baptised at graaff-reinet - - · barry the other missing barry child, and he is invisible for the opposite reason to his sister. she has no surname in the index; he has the same name as his brother. william fredrik barry was born 23 august 1853 and baptised at burgersdorp; this william frederick thomas was born 29 september 1861 and baptised at graaff-reinet, eight years later, to the same parents - "margaret wilhelmina kolbe + john barry". a search for william barry returns the 1853 child and stops, and nothing in the result says there is a second. by this family's own practice the first william must have died - a baptism is not done twice, which is exactly what this archive concluded about the two catherine mary sophias. the "william who appears on nothing else" on his mother's death notice is one of these two and the notice does not say which. ark:/61903/1:1:623r-9mm9 and 1:1:62gj-sd8z.

q: catherine mary sophia barry of 1855 10 jul 1855, baptised 22 jul 1855 at burgersdorp - bef. aug 1859 · barry the tenth child, found by reading 267 register images - and she has the same name as her sister. burgersdorp doopregister, image group 008039088, image 427: born 10 july 1855, baptised 22 july 1855, father john barry, mother margaret louisa kolbe. four years later the same parents baptised another catharina mary sophia at dordrecht, born 4 august 1859 - the woman who married into the booyzens and carried the name to australia. two daughters, one name, different birthdays four years apart in different towns. a baptism is not done twice, so the ordinary reading is the ordinary cape practice: this child died, and the name was given again. this archive has no burial for her and states the death only as "before august 1859". and she explains the name twice over: the archive has already shown catherine maria sophia is a kolbe name, off the 1848 godmother catharine sophia maria kolber. it was thought important enough to use, lose, and use again. 

george augustus kolbe of bethulie 1869 - - · kolbe taken prisoner in 1901, aged 32, at sterkfontein in the bethulie district, and recorded as a free stater. tna wo 108/368 folio 581. sent to natal. the second man of that name in the same list - the first being george augustus kolbe of burgersdorp, whom this archive identified from the wakkerstroom stones. bethulie is on the orange river, in the country the settler preached across. and thirteen years later a g. a. kolbe of bethulie is president of the orange free state agricultural association. the british press, 26 june to 22 july 1914: "mr. g. a. kolbe (bethulie)" in the delegate list printed by the daily telegraph; "mr g. a. kolbe, president of the orange free state agricultural association and chairman of the orange free state delegation" at the royal agricultural society's show, in the western daily press, dundee courier, cork free press and exeter and plymouth gazette of 2 july; and on 22 july the daily malta chronicle has him sending a telegram of respectful greeting to queen wilhelmina on the delegation's behalf. same initials, same district, thirteen years apart - from a prisoner's number to the head of the free state's farmers. no descent from the settler is claimed here.

q: a werdmuller child of 1857 14 feb 1857, baptised 10 apr 1857 at burgersdorp - - · kolbe and by the afternoon there was a candidate for the missing name. the queenstown free press of 13 february 1884 marries "charles andrew werdmuller, of steynsburg, second son of the late c.j.o. werdmuller, of burghersdorp" to charlotte anne callaghan. a man born 14 february 1857 was twenty-seven that week. not proved: no document read here names charles andrew's mother, and his father - or a man of exactly that name - married again at burgersdorp in 1874. nameless in the index, and that is the point. the same sweep that found the tenth barry child turned up a second entry with an empty name column: born 14 february 1857, baptised 10 april 1857 at burgersdorp, mother augusta louisa kolbe, father coenraad johannes otto werdmuller. she is the settler's fourth daughter, born at graaff-reinet in 1829 - and this is the first of her children this archive has ever seen. the child's own name is on the page and not in the index, so no search will ever return it. the register image has not been read; only the index line. 

g.a. kolbe of piet retief 23 feb 1836 - 7 jan 1913, piet retief · kolbe a date for the twin, if it is him. the stone at piet retief reads "vader en moeder - g.a. kolbe - geb. 23 feb. 1836 - overl. 7 jan. 1913 - a.m. kolbe - geb. 4 mei 1843 - overl. 21 sep. 1907 - van hun kinders". the settler's ninth and tenth children were twins born at burgersdorp in 1836, charlotte felicia and george augustus, and this archive has never had a day for either. a g.a. kolbe born 23 february 1836 is exactly the right man in exactly the right year - and it would date his twin sister too. it is initials and a year, not a name and a parent, and this archive has spent today being careful about exactly this. it would also give the other george augustus kolbe - born burgersdorp 2 october 1861, dead standerton 1934, buried wakkerstroom - a plausible father aged twenty-five, which is the shape the eastern transvaal kolbes have been missing.

s: 7 Jul 1822, Uitenhage – 3 Apr 1868, the farm Leeuwberg — aged 45 · Kolbe
q: john gerson eliezar kolbe 7 jul 1822, uitenhage - 3 apr 1868, the farm leeuwberg - aged 45 · kolbe the settler's eldest child, and until today a line in a table. his obituary - grahamstown journal, 15 april 1868, headed "death of commandant kolbe" - gives the whole man. born 7 july 1822; married 3 april 1843 to anna jacoba van der merwe; died 3 april 1868, on his wedding anniversary, at the farm leeuwberg, of typhus or typhoid caught on commando - "thus adding another to the long list of victims of our miserable war". he had settled on kaalspruit about 1850 and lies there - and he confirms the farm himself. a lost-property advertisement he placed in the friend on 9 march 1864 is signed "j.g.e. kolbe, kafferberg, kaalspruit" (the address as the paper printed it). the friend's own obituary transcription reads "[randspruit]", bracketed by the transcriber as doubtful; the man's own address settles it. that advertisement also puts the two brothers in one document: it concerns "a promissory note, date 9th march 1864, drawn by george augustus kolbe in favor of j.g.e. kolbe, payable 4 months after date for £154 stg" - lost on the market square at bloemfontein. he left a widow and twelve children - "of the eight sons and four daughters he has left behind him", which is the friend of the free state's own wording and a count the grahamstown reprint drops. only one daughter was married and the youngest child was an infant; two sons had been serving with him in the field and "proved themselves amongst the bravest of our burghers". none of the twelve is named and none is in this archive. he was commandant of the district, a justice of the peace, a director of the bloemfontein bank and a deacon of the dutch reformed church, and he had spoken in the volksraad in may 1867. he had refused public life for twelve years after the abandonment, having protested the british withdrawal and applied to sir george clerk for compensation for his land so that he might leave with the troops; failing that, "he, like many more, had to cast his lot with the free state". and on his deathbed, in full possession of his senses, he told the doctor and the others present that this state had taken too much land from the basutos, that he had always thought so and had said so in the raad, and begged them to rescind the resolution and treat with the governor for an equitable boundary. 20 september 2026 - a historian's draft names him too, and names the war. the dsab entry on his father says the eldest son "j.g.e. kolbe (1822-68), was later op leeuberg naby bloemfontein woonagtig en het gedurende die tweede sotho-vrystaatoorlog roem verwerf as kommandant". both years match this archive to the year - born 7 july 1822, dead 3 april 1868 - and both were got from an obituary and an auction advertisement that the entry does not cite. it is the strongest of the nine places where that entry and this archive agree from different documents. and it names what killed him: the obituary said only "our miserable war"; the war was the second sotho-free state war. and he may be in the 1830 letter, aged eight. read from the file rather than from a mail preview, msb 751 encloses "a jacket & waistcoat for john & a further jacket also for him, tell him his old father has sent it him, & to make haste to fill them out". clothes for a growing child, sent from soho to the cape in august 1830, when this man was eight years old and the eldest son of the house. if it is him it is the earliest document in this archive that mentions him. "his old father" is the difficulty and is not glossed over - the writer is his grandfather, and this is an inference, not a reading. 

s: 29 Sep 1817, a military post in what became British Kaffraria – 23 Feb 1872, the Modder River road, district Bloemfontein · Kolbe
q: francis mccabe 29 sep 1817, a military post in what became british kaffraria - 23 feb 1872, the modder river road, district bloemfontein · kolbe the second husband, and the reason the commandant's widow is filed under the wrong surname in the free state estate index. landdrost of bloemfontein, son of dr patrick mccabe, a staff-assistant surgeon attached to the british army on the cape frontier; his mother rose died at bloemfontein on 1 august 1858, aged 72 years 3 months and 8 days. he married anna jacoba van der merwe about april 1871 - "his second wife, about ten months since" - and was dead within fifteen months. on the anniversary of the state's independence he had spent the day superintending the burghers' annual target shooting for the government prize; at a quarter past five he set off by spring-cart for the diamond fields meaning to sleep at his own farm "uitvlugt" on the modder river; at about half past seven, in deceptive moonlight and one hour's ride short of the farm of g.f. enslin, the cart went into a sluit washed out by the rains. he was dead of heart disease that evening. he left four sons and two daughters of his own and "a large family of step-children", which is a newspaper counting the commandant's twelve. his brother joseph, the well-known trader and traveller, had died in the interior in december 1865; his brother john died at bloemfontein in 1860. he was buried on the sunday afternoon at six o'clock, the coffin carried by the resident members of the volksraad and the principal government officers, with the state president and upwards of two hundred walking behind. 15 september, from the free state estate index. vab mhg c129: "mccabe, francis. eggenotes 1) maria petronella elisabetha antoinetta raath en 2) anna (gebore van der merwe)", 1872 - so he had a first wife and she has a name. and vab 1/3/1/12 bc11: "mccabe, francis. insolvente boedel", with the remark "bevat geen sterfkennis nie" - contains no death notice. the landdrost of bloemfontein, buried with the state president walking behind him and two hundred people after that, left an insolvent estate. his widow's own entry, m777, names both her husbands, so the remarriage is in the archives and not only in a newspaper. 

john kolbe the younger - - - · kolbe the first of the twelve this archive can put a hand on. the free state criminal court, october 1868: a horse thief drove off three animals from the farm springfield, ward upper modder-river, district bloemfontein - a black mare and foal belonging to "anna jacoba van der merwe, widow of late j.g.e. kolbe", a blue schimmel mare and foal belonging to "john kolbe, jun.", and a chestnut riding horse belonging to a man named jephts. six months after his father died he is holding stock in his own right beside his mother. he is named by initial and suffix only, and nothing else about him is known - but an eighth of the obituary's "eight sons" now has a document. in 1884 the friend reported that the eldest son of "mr. john kolbe", a boy of ten called little jannie, was struck dead by lightning on his father's farm five hours north of bloemfontein; the natal witness index carries the same death and names the father george. two papers, two fathers, and this archive will not choose. 

anna jacoba van der merwe - - - · kolbe she remarried, and her second husband is why she was hard to find. the free state archives hold her under a different surname: vab mhg m777 - "mccabe, anna jacoba. nooiensvan van der merwe. eggenote john gherson [kolbe]", 1896. widowed in 1868 with twelve children and dead twenty-eight years later as mrs mccabe. her husband's own estate is beside it - vab mhg k71, "kolbe, john gerson eleazar. eggenote anna jacoba (gebore van der merwe)", 1868. and the mccabe name is already in this archive: a rosa magdalena kolbe was baptised at bloemfontein in 1890 to frederik fortuna kolbe and maria petronella elizabeth antoinetta mccabe - a second kolbe-mccabe marriage in the same small free state world, and this archive does not yet know whether that is a coincidence. neither estate is read. m777 is the document that would name the twelve children. married john gerson eliezar kolbe on 3 april 1843 and was widowed on the same date twenty-five years later. she is the third van der merwe to marry into these families. 15 september 2026 - mccabe has a first name, a birth date and an office. he is francis mccabe, landdrost of bloemfontein, son of dr patrick mccabe, a staff-assistant surgeon attached to the british army on the cape frontier, born at one of the military posts in what is now british kaffraria on 29 september 1817. his obituary in the friend says he "married his second wife about ten months since - the widow of the late commandant j.g.e. kolbe, of kafirberg, near this town", and he died suddenly of heart disease on the modder river road on 23 february 1872, aged 54, leaving "a widow, four sons and two daughters, besides a large family of step-children". so: married 3 april 1843, widowed 3 april 1868 with twelve children, married again about april 1871, widowed again fifteen months later, and dead in 1896 under his name. for about eleven months there were eighteen children attached to one household. she was living at springfield, ward upper modder-river, district bloemfontein in october 1868, when a black mare and foal of hers were stolen - the court record that says so is the only document this archive has that shows her doing anything at all. 

s: — – 1882 — death notice KAB MOOC 6/9/187, 4160; will MOOC 7/1/431, 102 · Kolbe
q: coenraad johannes otto werdmuller - - 1882 - death notice kab mooc 6/9/187, 4160; will mooc 7/1/431, 102 · kolbe he is in the cape archives from 1854 to 1882 and he died in 1882, not merely "before february 1884". motions in the supreme court in 1854, 1855, 1872 and 1873; a trustee in other men's insolvent estates; and in 1882, gsc 2/1/1/41 no. 60, "charles andrew werdmuller and coenraad johannes otto werdmuller trading as c.a. werdmuller and company" - father and son in business together, in the year he died. his own death notice and will are both filed and neither is read. the man the settler's fourth daughter married, and until today a bracket after her name. he is at burgersdorp in april 1857, standing at a font with augusta louisa kolbe. he is at burgersdorp again on 7 july 1874, married by special licence by the rev. william cromar to elizabeth johanna catharine vorster - and the eastern province herald prints his name in full as coenraad johannes otto werdmuller d'elgg, which is the first time this archive has seen the von elgg written by anyone but a genealogist. he is dead by february 1884, when his second son marries as the son of "the late c.j.o. werdmuller of burghersdorp". whether augusta louisa was dead before 1874 this archive does not know. 

charles andrew werdmuller - - - · kolbe the dates now close around him, though no document yet names his mother. his father's first wife, augusta louisa kolbe, made a will in 1868 and died in 1873 - kab mooc 7/1/332 no. 205, "kolbe, augusta louisa, wife of coenraad johannes otto werdmuller van elgg", filed 1873 - and his father remarried on 7 july 1874. in 1882 charles andrew was in business with his father as c.a. werdmuller and company, and in february 1884 he married. a son of the 1874 marriage would have been seven and nine. he can only be a child of the first marriage, and the first wife is the settler's daughter. the one loophole left is an earlier wife before augusta louisa, and his father's 1882 death notice would close it by naming the children. second son of the late c.j.o. werdmuller of burghersdorp, married at wesley church, queenstown, on 13 february 1884 to charlotte anne callaghan, eldest daughter of hugh callaghan of ashby manor. of steynsburg then, and by 1909 charles werdmuller, j.p., of hoopstad in the orange river colony - the town his wife died in. his mother is not named on anything read here. if he is the child born 14 february 1857 at burgersdorp he is augusta louisa kolbe's son and a grandson of the 1820 settler; if he belongs to his father's 1874 marriage he is no relation at all, and a man marrying in 1884 as a second son cannot be. the dates favour kolbe and the documents do not say it. 

s: 1829, Graaff-Reinet – 1873 — death notice KAB MOOC 6/9/145, 9981 · Kolbe
q: augusta louisa kolbe 1829, graaff-reinet - 1873 - death notice kab mooc 6/9/145, 9981 · kolbe the settler's fourth daughter has three documents and this archive had none of them. a will, made in 1868 and filed in 1873: kab mooc 7/1/332 no. 205, "kolbe, augusta louisa. wife of coenraad johannes otto werdmuller van elgg" - which is the first document read here that ties her to that man by anything but a newspaper. a death notice, mooc 6/9/145 no. 9981, 1873. and a liquidation and distribution account, mooc 13/1/299 no. 93, 1874, which means there was something to distribute. she died in 1873 and her husband remarried in july 1874 - a year and a month, which is what a widower does, and which settles the question this archive left open yesterday about whose son charles andrew is. none of the three is read. 

frederick fortunatus werdmuller - - 1953 - estate kab mooc 6/9/20496, 115/53 · kolbe the fortunatus name in a fourth surname. "petition of frederick fortunatus werdmuller of malmesbury", cape supreme court, 1907, twice in one year, both times in other men's insolvent estates; and an estate of his own in 1953. this archive has already followed frederik fortunatus from kolbe (1839) to barry (1863) to booysen (1899); here it is again, on a werdmuller - and augusta louisa kolbe married a werdmuller. 17 september 2026 - he is shown to be her son, and the sentence above is withdrawn. the last 214 images of the burgersdorp baptism register hold his font: fredrik fortunatus steenkamp werdmuller, born 25 april 1861, baptised 19 may 1861 at burgersdorp, father coenraad johannes otto werdmuller, mother augusta louisa kolbe - familysearch 1:1:6fw6-wxgs, image 673. the settler's fourth daughter gave her child her brother's name, which is how frederik fortunatus reached a fourth surname. and it dates augusta louisa: she was bearing her husband's children in 1861, thirteen years before he married again at burgersdorp in 1874 - which bears directly on whether charles andrew was her son. the one step not taken: that the child of 1861 is the man of the 1907 petition and the 1953 estate. both are frederick fortunatus werdmuller at the cape and the name is rare; the 1907 man is of malmesbury and the child was baptised at burgersdorp, and no document read here joins them. 

s: c. 1859 – 17 Feb 1891, Hoopstad, Orange Free State — aged 32 · Kolbe
q: charlotte anne callaghan c. 1859 - 17 feb 1891, hoopstad, orange free state - aged 32 · kolbe eldest daughter of hugh callaghan, esq., of ashby manor, district of queenstown; married charles andrew werdmuller on 13 february 1884. seven years later she was dead at thirty-two, at hoopstad, "after a long illness", and a correspondent's obituary in the queenstown free press adds that she had arrived there only a few months before, in indifferent health, with a disorder of the heart that proved organic. she left "a husband and two little girls", and it is that line which lets the 1909 marriage notice call amy a second daughter. 

amy werdmuller - - - · kolbe "martineau - werdmuller - on july 31 [1909], at east london, horace robert martineau, v.c., of durban, to amy werdmuller, second daughter of charles werdmuller, j.p. of hoopstad, o.r.c." one of the two little girls her mother left in 1891. if the chain holds - and it has one unproved link, her grandmother's name - she is a great-granddaughter of the 1820 settler, and she married a holder of the victoria cross. this archive prints the two letters as the journal printed them and has not gone looking for which action he won it for.

mary elizabeth kolbe - - bef. 23 oct 1863 - intestate · kolbe her death is now dated, and she died without a will. the friend of the free state, 23 october 1863, twice in two weeks: "derwyl maria elizabeth kolbe zonder testament na te laten is overleden en de nagebleven echtgenoot g.f. enslin by brieve van administratie ter vereffening van haren boedel als executeur is aangesteld" - she had died intestate and her husband was appointed executor of her estate. this archive had only "before 1867", inferred. it is now before 23 october 1863, from a notice her own husband placed. margaretha's sister, and the woman who married george frederick enslin - which is the whole answer to a contradiction this archive carried as serious, that margaretha appeared to marry enslin while married to john barry. it was resolved from margaret downing's 1867 death notice. the burgersdorp register of 23 october 1853 shows it instead: the two sisters baptising a son each, two entries apart, on one page.

q: william barry 23 aug 1853, baptised 23 oct 1853 at burgersdorp - - · barry found twice in one day. he came in on the 1915 death notice of his mother margaretha kolbe, estate 1291, which names nine children where his father's names eight - and then the burgersdorp doopregister produced his baptism: william fredrik, born 23 august 1853, christened 23 october, godparents john kolbe, anna van der merwe and george kolbe. two of the three are his mother's brothers. a second william frederick thomas was baptised in 1861 and this archive cannot say whether the first died or a clerk erred - a doubt re-surfaced, and briefly mistaken for a new find, when the index was asked for every barry child of a kolbe mother. he is not on his father's notice, not on the cape rebel roll, and nowhere else in this archive. his father's 1903 registration said eleven children; with william there are nine named and two still missing.

johan gottlieb kolbe c. 1764 - 18 nov 1845, london · kolbe he had eight sons, and this archive knew of one. his son's obituary in the grahamstown journal of 19 december 1844 calls george augustus "the last remaining of eight sons of john godloff kolbe esq. of brunswick-square, london". seven brothers, all dead before december 1844, none of them named anywhere in this archive - and dead men do not appear in a census, which is why the 1841 conduit street household holds three women and no sons. the obituary also puts him at brunswick square, in bloomsbury, where the census and the death put him at conduit street in mayfair, a mile and a half away. both can be true twenty years apart, and this archive has already moved this man once - off the family tree's lamb's conduit street - so it records a second address rather than making a second correction. "esq.", not "tailor". and he is in the london gazette, nine years before he died: issue 19424, page 1702, 29 september 1836, dissolving the copartnership of "john gottlob kolbe and david fletcher, of conduit-street, bond-street, in the county of middlesex, tailors". that is his trade, his street and a business partner, in print, from a free source - and it pushes him back to conduit street in 1836. and the death is now a gro reference: freebmd gives one kolbe death in all of england and wales for 1845-46 - "deaths dec 1845, kolbe, john gottlob, st geo han sq, vol 1, page 35". the district matches the census; the name form john gottlob matches his son's 1803 baptism; and the certificate, not yet ordered, would name the informant. found in the 1841 census, which settles two things this archive had argued from other documents. he is at conduit street, st george hanover square, sub-district may fair, aged 76 - four years before he died at number 34, and independent of the death record that corrected the family tree's lamb's conduit street. and his birth county is entered as "foreign", which is the first document in this archive to say in its own words that he was not english. ho107, piece 734, book 1, folio 11, page 15, schedule 38. three women share that schedule: marianne, 35, charlotte, 30, and amelia a., 25. tailor. died at 34 conduit street, mayfair - not lamb's conduit street; the tree's photograph is of the wrong building. 16 september 2026 - the address argument is over, and he had two wives. the westminster rate books index him one hundred and twenty-one times between 1800 and 1831, under twenty-four spellings of his forename - gothel, gotleb, gotleib, gotlieb, gotliel, gotlob, gotlobe, goltief, gottieb, gottiel, gottlieb, gottlob, gutlieb, kottieb, gilliet and once "jos gottiel". in 1800 he is at broad street north, st james piccadilly, folio 41 - which independently corroborates the printed 1799 list of 234 master tailors, "kolbe, john, 18 broad-street, soho". from 1811 to 1831 he is at church street south, st anne's soho, year after year, and the 1829 land tax return says the same. brunswick square appears in no rate book, no land tax return, no census and no burial register - those are westminster sources and bloomsbury would not be in them, so they cannot disprove it, but soho 1800-1831, st george hanover square in 1841 and a death there in 1845 leaves no window for it. and the burial is now a register entry rather than a tree claim: westminster burials, city of westminster archives centre - died 18 november 1845, buried 26 november 1845 at st john the baptist, great marlborough street, page 7, year of birth given as 1764. the date matches the tree's "26 november 1845, entry 55, grave 7" to the day and the "7" matches; the church does not. 20 september 2026 - he writes, and he signs himself. msb 751 at the national library of south africa is a letter of four sides headed "london august 23. 1830", opening "dear george" and signed "your affectionate father, j g kolbe". it is the first document in this archive he wrote himself - everything else is somebody writing about him. it does not carry a street address: the heading is "london" and nothing finer, so it does not settle brunswick square against conduit street, which is what this archive most hoped for. what it does carry: his son's acceptance by the london missionary society in the father's own words, dr philip carrying an earlier letter to the cape, mr miles of the society calling at the house, henry dying of dropsy and "resigned to the catastrophe", milne and elizabeth - "betsey" - removed to edinburgh, charlotte sending an evangelical magazine, a suit of black clothes sent out for a newly accepted missionary, the death of george iv and the french revolution of july 1830 as fresh news, and a request that his son fact-check a baboon story in a magazine. and the line that counts most: "kind love from your sisters & brother" - sisters plural, brother singular. of the eight sons, two were alive in august 1830. 20 september, read again from the file instead of from a mail preview, and it carries more. dr philip is not just the courier - "dr philip was exceedingly glad to hear of you being accepted by the l.m.s. as you may well imagine, he has promised to write to you a letter by the first opportunity". he sends a box: a suit of black clothes for george, and a jacket and waistcoat for john with a further jacket, "tell him his old father has sent it him, & to make haste to fill them out". a year of newspapers, one number lost by henry. and the house has friends with names, the first in this archive who simply knew them: mr & mrs stanhope, mr and mrs warner, and mrs field and her daughters - "the eldest, miss mary, that was, has married a mr bellew, a surgeon". two of his four pages go on a story from the mirror about a scottish colonist near the xhosa whose wife was carried off by orang-outangs and recovered after two years as their queen - and he does not believe a word of it: "here we look upon the story as a fictious & romance… i should be glad to hear from you, whether that report may be founded in truth, or falsehood." a tailor of seventy, reading a cheap weekly, writing to the one man he knew who was actually there to ask whether it was true. his first wife mary died 2 august 1814 aged 46 and his second, also mary, died 15 august 1824 aged 36, both buried in the german lutheran church register, tna rg 4/4631 - which is why one mary could never be made to fit a run of baptisms from 1792 to 1819. and the london gazette holds five notices, not the one this archive had. 12 may 1824 - the partnership of john gotlob kolbe and john henry kolbe, of church-street, soho, tailors, dissolved. 30 september 1836 - kolbe and david fletcher of conduit-street dissolved. 21 march 1845 - "john gotlieb kolbe and richard davies, of conduit-street, bond-street, tailors, has been dissolved by mutual consent", eight months before he died and still calling himself a tailor, which is what the obituary's "esq. of brunswick-square" has to be set against. 1824 was the year it all went: the partnership dissolved in may, his second wife dead in august, and his son in the insolvent debtors' lists in october and november. 16 september, later - and the 1799 tailors' list has a twin. in april and may 1834 the london press printed the roll of "considerably more than three hundred of the master tailors of the metropolis" who met at willis's rooms, st james's-street, to resist the grand national consolidated trades' union, and the entry reads "kolbe and fletcher, conduit-street" - morning post 30 april, globe 30 april and 10 may, old england 4 may, morning herald 10 may, london courier 10 may, true sun 10 may, public ledger 12 may. seven newspapers, one line. 20 september 2026 - and a historian called him an apothecary. the dsab draft entry on his son opens "die seun van j.g.kolbe, 'n duitse apteker wat in londen woonagtig was". the german is right and the london is right and the trade is his son's - george augustus sailed in 1820 as an apothecary, and the apothecary has been handed back up to the father. it is the only thing in that entry this archive can show to be wrong, and it can only show it because it read the rate books. it closes the gap: the rate books had him in soho to 1831 and the gazette at conduit street by 1836; he was at conduit street, with fletcher, by 29 april 1834. and it rhymes with the first list thirty-five years earlier - in december 1799 one of 234 masters over the combination acts, a young man at 18 broad-street; in april 1834 a firm with a partner and a bond street address, seventy years old, on the masters' side of the same argument.

s: bapt. 29 Jul 1800, St James, Westminster – 13 Apr 1832, buried 22 Apr 1832, German Lutheran Church · Kolbe
q: john henry kolbe bapt. 29 jul 1800, st james, westminster - 13 apr 1832, buried 22 apr 1832, german lutheran church · kolbe one of the eight sons, and the one who lived longest of those found. baptised 29 july 1800, father john, mother mary, batch i02559-1. tna rg 4/4631 folio 100: died 13 april 1832, buried 22 april, aged 32 - twelve years before the obituary that counted him among the seven already gone. and he speaks. old bailey, session of 13 january 1819, trial t18190113-149 - richard kerr indicted for stealing "one coat, value 6l., the property of john henry kolbe". his own deposition: "my father is a tailor, and lives in church-street, soho. on the 9th of january, about eleven o'clock at night, i stopped at the star and crown public-house, westminster, and left my coat over my horse's head - i had a chaise standing at the door; i saw the prisoner go out, and suspected him - i went out, and missed my coat." not guilty. he was eighteen, and his brother george augustus sailed for algoa bay the following year. it is the only voice this archive has from the soho house, and it corroborates the rate books' address from a source that had no interest in it. and the london gazette says what became of him. 12 may 1824, issue 18027 page 796: the partnership of "john gotlob kolbe and john henry kolbe, of church-street, soho, in the county of middlesex, tailors" dissolved - father and son, in business together, at the address he gave the court five years earlier. then 9 october and 16 november 1824, issues 18069 page 1668 and 18080 page 1900, in the insolvent debtors lists, petitions to be heard at portugal-street, lincoln's-inn fields on 5 november: "kolbe, john henry (sued as henry kolbe), formerly of no. 22, norfolk-street, middlesex-hospital, and late of no. 4, mansfield-place". he was twenty-four, out of the family business and out of soho in the same year his stepmother died, and he was dead at thirty-two. 20 september 2026 - and his father writes about his dying. msb 751, the letter of 23 august 1830 to his brother at the cape: "henry had wrote to you himself & left his letter at the mission house to be forwarded to you… he keeps up pretty well at present, but what effect the winter may have upon him if it should set in very cold, as it did last winter, is perhaps not doubtful, since it must prevent him from taking exercise by walking, & which is a great means of keeping down the dropsy, of which he bears still the symptoms… i trust also that you will join your prayers, that he may vouchsafe to prepare him to a fit state of meeting his god… he appears at present to be resigned to the catastrophe." he had twenty months left. and the same letter's closing - "kind love from your sisters & brother" - makes him the last of the eight sons alive besides george augustus, so that the obituary's "last remaining of eight sons" became true on 13 april 1832, twelve years before it was printed. and he married three months after the trial: westminster marriages - john henry kolbe and matilda ford, 26 april 1819, st margaret westminster, both of that parish. he was eighteen. a mary ann maria ford kolbe married at whitechapel in the first quarter of 1847 - gro index volume az, 840, page 16 - and "ford" carried as a forename is how families carried a mother's maiden name. she is very probably his daughter. and the press gives his trade, which the gazette did not. law chronicle, commercial and bankruptcy register, 13 january 1825: "kolbe john henry, of norfolk-street, middlesex-hospital, last of mansfield-st., kentish town, tailor, draper" - so he set up on his own account in his father's trade, and the gazette's "mansfield-place" is mansfield street, kentish town. the may 1824 dissolution was reported in at least six london papers, all of them putting his name first: "j. h. kolbe and j. g. kolbe, church-street, soho, tailors". and the 1830 letter shows him doing an ordinary thing. packing a year of newspapers for the cape, his father notes one number missing - "the one of the 4th of decr last, which cannot be found, supposing that henry, who has them every week, after i have done with them, - has lost". the father read the paper first and the son had it after. it is the only description this archive has of what anybody in that house did with an ordinary evening, and he had four months to live when it was written.

frederick kolbe of 1816 bapt. 16 dec 1816, westminster - - · kolbe right surname, right parish, right decade, and a gap in the family's own baptism run exactly there. he is not a brother. his father is george and his mother elizabeth, and his register batch is c72301-7 rather than the family's c15051-2 or c06236-1. he was one click from being made an eighth son, and what stopped it was reading the parents' names on the transcript instead of the name, place and year in the result list. the same check threw out henry kolbe, baptised at southwark on 2 february 1800 - father henry, mother susannah. and the rejection turned out not to be a dead end. morning advertiser, 31 december 1832: "left his home, monday, december 10, frederick kolbe, about 16, dark hair and eyes, with an impediment in his sight. any information addressed mrs. kolbe, no. 18, gerrard-street, soho, will be rewarded; if he will return, will…" - and a boy "about 16" in december 1832 is one baptised in december 1816. gerrard street is two streets from church street. there were two kolbe households in soho at once, and every soho kolbe record on this site has to be read against that. whether the two families were related is not known here. 

marianne kolbe 1806 - - · kolbe aged 35 and living with her father johan gottlieb in conduit street at the 1841 census, schedule 38. almost certainly a sister of george augustus, who had sailed for the cape twenty-one years earlier and never came back. from the census - no baptism has been read for her. 17 september 2026 - and the reason is now sharper. the eleven known children of the house leave gaps at 1808-1812 and 1814-1818, and the 1841 ages of the three women in it - rounded down to the nearest five, so born about 1802-06, 1807-11 and 1812-16 - fall in and around those gaps. the same two gaps the three missing sons must sit in. the 1841 census records no relationships, that column beginning in 1851, so her place in this family is an inference from living in the house. the savoy baptism register would settle it and is locked. 

charlotte kolbe 1811 - 1867, lambeth - probably · kolbe aged 30 in the conduit street household at the 1841 census. from the census. 17 september 2026 - she is not in the 1851 census and she probably did not die before it. there are only four kolbe deaths in all england and wales between 1837 and 1867 - john gottlob 1845, george 1848, elizabeth 1852 and charlotte kolbe at lambeth in 1867. the single kolbe in the entire 1851 census is also at lambeth. if the 1867 death is hers she outlived her father by twenty-two years and was simply not caught by the 1851 enumerator under this surname. 20 september 2026 - she is no longer an inference. this record was marked `inf` because she matched no baptism in the family's own register run and her place in the house was read off a census that records no relationships. msb 751, her father's letter of 23 august 1830: "charlotte sends you an evangelical magazine, with the account of the death of the rev. w. orme, late secretary to the l.m.s." her father names her sending a magazine to her brother. she is a daughter of this house on the evidence of the house.

s: 7 Dec 1802, Soho — baptised 2 Feb 1803, Westminster – 1 Dec 1844, “Wurtemburg”, Colesberg · Kolbe
q: george augustus kolbe 7 dec 1802, soho - baptised 2 feb 1803, westminster - 1 dec 1844, "wurtemburg", colesberg · kolbe his obituary is found, eighteen days after the death: grahamstown journal, 19 december 1844. "died at his farm, wirtemberg, near the orange river, december 1st, the rev. george augustus kolbe, aged 44 years, a man possessed of a most amiable temper, and of more than ordinary abilities. he was the last remaining of eight sons of john godloff kolbe esq. of brunswick-square, london, has left a widow and ten children... he having been for many years engaged in rendering them medical advice and assistance whenever called upon... his disease was an affection on the lungs." eight sons, seven of them dead before december 1844 and not one in this archive. brunswick square, which is not conduit street and is a mile and a half from it. a man who doctored a district for thirty years, where his own death notice says only "agriculturist". and a cause of death, after nearly a year ill. the notice also says 44 when he was 41, and ten children when this archive counts eleven living - it is the best kind of source and it is not a register. 1820 settler - the nautilus, owen's party, algoa bay 14 apr 1820. married at sixteen on a sworn falsehood. preached across the orange river. his grandson could not name him in 1915. 15 september - he was an lms missionary, and his father wrote to him. the south african library at cape town holds msb751, the ga kolbe collection, donated by dr jean griffiths of somerset west in 1985: "george augustus kolbe, pharmacist, 1820 settler, missionary, married margaret downing" and, on a second entry, "george augustus kolbe, 1802-44. lms missionary." it corroborates a memory this archive published the same morning as an inference - john montgomery's recollection of a bushman mission school at koolskop about 1824, where colesberg now stands. two sources with nothing to do with each other, agreeing. the collection is four photocopied pages containing a letter of 23 august 1830 from johan kolbe in london to his son - the only known document connecting the tailor of conduit street to the settler of colesberg. it has now been read, and it does not carry a street address. the catalogue called it a letter "on his ordination" and this archive repeated the catalogue; it is not. 20 september 2026 - and a second attachment came with it. a two-page afrikaans typescript headed "msb 751 / [konsep] vir dsab / voorlopige teks", initialled ks and dated 18/2/92 - a draft entry for the dictionary of south african biography, by dr karel schoeman, on the word of the national library that holds the file: "the author, ks, would be dr. karel schoeman who worked here at the national library". it is a secondary work and this archive does not take secondary works as evidence - but it agrees with this archive on nine points reached by nine other roads (the 1802 birth, j.g.e. kolbe 1822-68 at leeuberg as a commandant, margaret downing 1803-1867, the 1819 london marriage, the apothecary's trade, the farm wurthemberg, ten children, philippolis from march 1831) and it is wrong about exactly one thing: it calls his father a german apothecary. he was a tailor, on 121 rate books, two printed masters' lists, three gazette notices, the census, the burial register and his other son's sworn deposition. the trade is the son's, moved one generation up. what the entry adds, all of it untested: the graaff-reinet missionary society from about 1824, working among the slaves of the district; acceptance as an lms mission assistant on 8 february 1828 and posting to boesmanskool - the present bethulie - with james clark among the san; a journey with melvill to the caledon valley in november 1828, as far as present-day ladybrand, the earliest journey in the present free state of which a written record survives, and printed under his own name in the transactions of the missionary society for 1829 - a second document he wrote himself, searched for and not found; philippolis from march 1831, alone after melvill left in march 1832; ordination on 25 may 1833 by the french missionaries arbousset and casalis; his advice behind the berlin missionary society's founding of bethanie in 1834; an accusation of adultery in 1836 with the wife of one of his congregation, agitated by h. hendricks, secretary of the griqua council - an inquiry by the french missionaries acquitted him - continued opposition from t. atkinson, withdrawal from the station in march 1837 and dismissal by the lms on 19 june 1837; the farm driefontein near philippolis; and thirteen children, not eleven - ten left, only eight on the death notice, three dead as infants. it also settles the farm name: "wurthemberg, sometimes also given as knapdaar", which is a second name to search. and it names a portrait: a likeness of him as a young man, in 1992 with c.j. du plessis of ruigtevlei, district bethulie, reproduced in olivier (1973); and a charles bell watercolour of a church service at philippolis in 1834 with kolbe in the pulpit, in the africana museum, johannesburg. this archive holds no likeness of anybody born before 1850. there may be two of this man. and he wrote something else, and it is findable. the 1829 journal extract the dsab cites is catalogued under the other man's name, which is why a search for kolbe found nothing: "extracts of the journal of messrs melvill and kolbe, addressed to the rev. richard miles, superintendent of the society's missions in africa, philippolis, 25 nov. 1828", in the council for world missions archive at soas - which is source 4 on the dsab's own list, two lines above source 6. an edited version dated 18 november 1828 appears in melvill (1829), and the journey is printed entire in karel schoeman (ed.), early white travellers in the transgariep, 1819-1840 (protea, 2003), p. 30. legassick quotes him: on the caledon they met people with "no other means of subsistence than the wild animals found in these parts". the first words of his this archive has read, and they are about famine. and the man he addressed it to is very probably the man who called at his father's house: richard miles was sent to cape town to act as dr philip's substitute while philip was in england, which puts him at the cape in 1828 and back in london by 1830. the 1830 letter says only "mr miles", so this is an identification and not a document. and one of them is catalogued, in scotland: university of edinburgh, centre for the study of world christianity, cswc 60 - five photograph copies of bell sketches of african congregations, item 3 "mr. kolbe… at philippolis in 1834". edinburgh calls him "a moravian missionary?", question mark and all; he was london missionary society, and this archive has his father's letter saying so. the dsab puts the original watercolour in johannesburg and never mentions scotland; edinburgh never mentions johannesburg. 

s: 23 Feb 1803, London – 2_ Nov 1867, Burgersdorp — the day illegible on the stone · Downing
q: margaret downing 23 feb 1803, london - 2_ nov 1867, burgersdorp - the day illegible on the stone · downing the answer was on a photograph this archive has had all along. the burgersdorp monument is on the kolbe page, and the caption quoted it as far as "also his relict margaret downing…" and stopped there. the stone goes on: "born in london 23 february 1803 and died at burghersdorp 2_ november 1867." her birth is now a date - 23 february 1803, where this archive had "c. 1804" - and the death is settled at 1867. her son's obituary of 15 april 1868 said she had died "about three months since", which would have been january 1868; it was nearly five months, and a journalist rounding is a journalist rounding. the day is a 2 and a digit that will not resolve at any magnification, and is not guessed. the cape estate ran on: mooc 13/1/253 no. 2, "downing, margaret, widow of kolbe, george augustus. liquidation and distribution account", 1869 - and she had made a will of her own in 1854, mooc 7/1/295 no. 70, ten years after she was widowed. married at fifteen in shoreditch, signing with a mark. died owning a house and a farm. 20 september 2026 - and there is a certificate, in a museum. the dsab draft on her husband lists among its sources "albany museum, grahamstad: fotokopie van die huwelikssertifikaat van g.a. kolbe (1819)". this archive holds the allegation and not the marriage - the sworn statement made to get the licence, which is where the false age was sworn, and not the register entry that followed it. a photocopy of the certificate has been sitting in grahamstown since before 1992. the same entry gives her dates as "(1803-1867)", which is what the burgersdorp stone says, from a source that had not read the stone this way.
